rendered:
1. Coprecipitation window: the NFA hydroxide precursors must be coprecipitated within a pH window between 10 and 12[1]. The reason is that the metals do not precipitate together. Simultaneous coprecipitation of nickel, iron and aluminum is hard because their hydroxides have different solubility products. hydroxides of aluminum start precipitating[2] at a lower pH value when compared to hydroxides of nickel[3], while the nickel and iron hydroxides precipitate beyond pH 6[4]. This narrows the usable window to the range above. In practice the reactor is held at the upper part of the window: to maintain the pH to above 10 especially for nickel-[5], with NaOH pumped in during continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) operation. The document does not explain why the window stops at its upper limit.

2. From precursor to cathode powder: the outflow from the reactor is filtered, washed, and dried[6] to obtain the hydroxide precursors. These are then mixed with a lithium source (Li2CO3, LiOH, LiNO3, etc.)[7] and calcined in an O2-rich environments at temperatures[8] >600 °C[9]. After calcination the NFA cathode powder is cast into electrodes by a roll-to-roll slot-die coating process[10], followed by pouch cell assembly, formation and cycling.
